rv.q: Paul is at once mythic (for the world of the play is one in which record companies underwrite acts to an extent unseen for decades in the real world) and, through the cracks in the icon, still vestigially human.
Andrew Scott's extraordinary performance lights up Simon Stephens's new play about a rock god losing his mind.
I left the theatre with a taste of disappointment on my tongue.

cn.t: Andrew Scott delivers an extraordinary performance as a imploding rock star in Simon Stephens's new play, but the familiar tale of fame's destabilizing effects proves more tame than unnerving despite inventive staging.
